summary: American pulp writer L. Ron Hubbard fabricated a heroic life story, launched Dianetics in 1950, turned it into the Church of Scientology, and ran an abusive private fleet, the Sea Org, from 1967 to 1975.

evidence.note: Dianetics book published May 1950, the first consequential act
kidnaps daughter Alexis and physically abducts and chokes wife Sara
flies with the baby to Havana, Cuba, and writes there
moves to England, buys a manor house as a training base
fleet assembles at Las Palmas, Canary Islands; later Valencia
fleet based at Corfu under the Greek junta until expelled
Morocco courted as headquarters before fleet flees
young boy locked in the chain locker for two days
Warning: Susan Meister's suicide aboard the Apollo described
story ends with 1975 move ashore to Clearwater; later years skipped

notes: Story stops at 1975; covered_span extended to 1986 only by the lifetime rule. main_span set 1950-1986 (Dianetics to death); 1934 pulp career start was an alternative. Brief modern Scientology mentions (Narconon, squirrel busters) judged too short for reaches_present. Host says net worth six million in part 1 but 600 million in part 3.
